investor

in-VES-ter · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A person who puts money into a business or plan, hoping to get more money back.

An investor gave the bike shop money to help it open a second store.

Example

Grandma became an investor in Leo's lemonade stand: she paid for the lemons, and he shared what the stand earned.

Grandma put her own money in first, and got money back later when the stand did well. Putting money in and hoping for more back is what an investor does.

How Strong Is It?

fan → investor → owner

fan vs. investor

fan vs. investor: A fan is the weaker word: a fan only hopes a business does well, while an investor puts real money into it and can lose that money.

owner vs. investor

owner vs. investor: An owner goes further than an investor: an investor puts money into a business and holds a small part, while an owner holds the whole business and runs it.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — invest: to put money into something

suffix — or: a person who does it

Put it together: Investor is just invest plus -or, 'a person who.' An actor is a person who acts; an investor is a person who invests.

Use the root in a new word: reinvest: Invest came into English from Latin, where investire meant 'to clothe' — an investor wraps money up in a plan and hopes it grows. Maya's lemonade stand made ten dollars, and she decided to reinvest it in more lemons and cups.

Word Choice

You will hear investor in news about big companies, but anyone can be one - even a kid who puts allowance money into a friend's sticker stand.
